survivors.argument:

Mutant: -> true, the case is selected, subject `x` is clean, `String.upcase(label)` is the continuation and spans line 5, so the rule emits `label =
  case x,
    do: (
      :ok -> label = "s"
      _ -> label = "u"
    )` - `rewrite_branches/2` cannot touch the wrapped branch list, so the inner assignments survive and only the wrapper changes. Source changed vs unchanged; `should_report?/2` flips false->true. Verified with a standalone simulation of the rule. (Same mutant also crashes the rule with Protocol.UndefinedError on `case(x, y)`, and rewrites `case x do IO.puts("hi") end`.)

`extract_do_branches/1` is private and has exactly one call site (line 185; grepped the whole lib/ tree).   case x do
    :ok -> ~c"s"
    _ -> ~c"u"

find_matching_end/2 returns {:ok, idx} or :error. Masking cannot manufacture the case either: SourceMask's @blank is 0x01, which matches neither `\w` nor `\s`, so the shadow never carries a word byte the source lacks.   def run do

      NIE.call()
    rescue
      e in [NotImplementedError, RuntimeError] -> e

end

survivors.argument: Column 77 is the `1` inside the SECOND arm of capture1?: `match?({:&, _, [{:__block__, _, [1]}]}, a)`. That arm is not dead code. Sourceror parses with a literal_encoder, and the bare `&1` token is emitted by the parser as `{:&, meta, [1]}` with the integer NOT passed through the encoder (verified) — that is what the first arm catches. But when the placeholder is written so that `&` applies to a parenthesized integer, the integer DOES go through the encoder and the node becomes `{:&, meta, [{:__block__, meta2, [1]}]}` — exactly the second arm's shape. `&((&(1)) != "")` is valid, compiling Elixir: its plain (encoder-free) AST is identical to that of `&(&1 != "")` — `{:&,_,[{:!=,_,[{:&,_,[1]},""]}]}` — and it evaluates identically (both give ["a","b"] on "a,,b"). With the literal at 1, empty_filter_call?/1 returns true: check/2 emits the issue and fix_patches/2 rewrites to `String.split(",", trim: true)`. With it mutated to 0, neither arm of capture1? matches (first arm wants an unwrapped 1, second now wants 0), capture2?/empty1? are false too, so empty_filter_call?/1 returns false and BOTH check and fix go silent. Simulated the predicate on the real Sourceror-shaped AST: literal=1 -> true, literal=0 -> false. The triplet misses it because all six fixtures write the bare `&1` token, which only ever exercises the first arm. (The opposite direction — mutant fires where original doesn't — is indeed blocked by CompileError, since `&0` is not a legal capture index; but the forward direction above is a genuine separating input, so this is a GAP, not an equivalence.)
survivors.separating_input:
sentence
|> String.split(",")
|> Enum.filter(&((&(1)) != ""))
